MEMORANDUM
  Agenda Item #: 7
  Meeting Date: 1-12-2022

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL MEMBERS

THRU:  SHARON PAPA, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  DEBORAH CHANKIN, INTERIM PUBLIC WORKS DIRECTOR

SUBJECT:  RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE PARKLANDS COMMITTEE
  FROM NOVMEBER 18, 2021

DATE:  JANUARY 12, 2021

ACTION REQUIRED  CONSENT  X  RECEIVE & FILE

Recommendation

Staff recommends that the City Council approve the actions of the Parklands Committee
from its meeting of November 18, 2021.

Summary

At the Parklands Committee meeting of November 18, 2021 all Committee Members were
present. Three applications were discussed and one application was pulled from the agenda
to a date uncertain.

Analysis and Findings

The City held a Parklands Committee meeting on November 18, 2021 and the Committee
recommended the following actions be approved by the City Council.

A request was presented from staff to continue Item No. 4 (PC-15-21) Concept Plan for
Malaga Dunes Restoration Project due to newly received information about the property
involved.

1. PC-558-21; Application to remove three Queen Palms located in the parkway adjacent
  to 2116 Paseo Del Mar.

  Applicant: Horist Construction, 3330 Kashiwa Street, Torrance, CA 90505
  1
 Three Queen Palm trees in the parkway requested for removal. Staff noted the designated street
tree is the Kentia palm. Staff advised the application did not specify, but staff assumed the
request was for site removal due to view obstruction from the second story balcony. The Urban
Forester noted the trees in the application were mature and provided the height and
circumference of two of the trees. The City has never maintained the trees because the
Parklands Committee approved the trees as part of a landscape plan in 1998 and it was intended
that the resident would maintain the landscape.

Staff provided pictures of the view corridors to the right and left of the Queen palms. Staff
advised that a large Senegal Date palm was removed earlier this year without approval. The
Senegal Date palm was adjacent to the three Queen palms in the center of the parkway. Staff
presented slides of the Senegal Date palm that was removed at various stages of size from 2011
to 2018, advising that when trees are removed without approval, restoration is required, citing
Chapter 12 of the Municipal Code and advising the cost for replacement. Staff showed pictures
of the neighborhood character noting several types of palm trees. The Queen palms designated
for removal are not the designated street tree, but they are in character with the neighborhood.
Staff recommended the Committee deny the request to remove the three Queen palms and direct
the Public Works Director to fix the restoration fee for the removal of the Senegal Date palm.

Thereafter, the Committee discussed the issue with the Urban Forester and asked clarifying
questions.

Public Hearing. Gordon Curtis representing the owners John and Judy Colich addressed the
Committee. A lengthy discussion ensued as to whether it was the Committee’s responsibility
to recommend restoration of the trees removed, or to pay fees to the tree bank; or to decide on
the removal of the three Queen palms and defer the restoration of the Senegal palms to the
Public Works Director. The committee members each expressed their opinion about what they
felt would cure the issue. The Public Hearing was closed.

Following the Public Hearing, further discussion continued regarding the removal of the three
Queen Palms.

ACTION: Moved by Member Cooper, and seconded by Committee Member Nye, to deny the
application to remove the three Queen palms and recommended the planting of four Kentia
palms designated street trees (Kentia palms-Howea foresteriana), each with 10 feet of brown
trunk, to be planted in the parkway as restoration for the Senegal Date palm that was removed.
The motion unanimously carried by the following by roll call vote.

  2. PC-559-21; Application to remove five trees located in the parkway adjacent to 4036
  Via Solano

The Urban Forester advised that the applicant would like to remove one Birch tree, two King
palms, a Kumquat tree, and a Peruvian Pepper tree. Staff advised that although not large, the
trees were mature. The Urban Forester advised the Committee that in considering the removal

  2
 of public vegetation for non-view related reasons, the Parklands Committee must seek a
reasonable balance between preservation and enhancement of mature trees and the protection
of privacy and the preservation and enhancement of public safety as outlined in Resolution R18-
13. He noted the designated street tree is the Guadalupe Palm, so the committee would want to
respect the neighborhood character and should not make a decision that would result in
significantly altering the unique feeling of the neighborhood.

Staff advised that the Birch tree, Kumquat tree, and the Pepper tree are not in character with the
neighborhood, but the King palms are somewhat in character with the other palms on the street.
Staff stated that preserving the King palms would not create a safety issue. Staff recommended
removal of the Birch tree, the Peruvian Pepper tree, and the Kumquat tree according to standard
conditions for tree removal approvals; and denial of the removal of the King palms. Staff
recommended the applicant be required to protect the King palms during construction; require
a payment of $1,500 to the tree bank, obtain a tree removal permit and removal of the stumps.

Public Hearing. Applicant Jim Schuchert addressed the Committee. Questions between
Committee Members, the applicant, and Staff regarding the trees in question and whether the
location of the driveway has been approved. The applicant advised that the driveway
application was continued to the November 30th Planning Commission meeting for approval.
The applicant stated he would prefer the removal of the King palms as well because he would
be planting mature Olive trees on his private property, but indicated a preference of keeping the
King palms over the Guadalupe palms. A lengthy discussion regarding the King palms and the
Guadalupe palms ensued. Discussion options for transplanting trees that are removed rather
than placing them in landfill.
After closing the Public Hearing, there was further discussion regarding removal of the trees
and the applicant showed a rendering of the completed home with the proposed landscape.

Action. It was moved by Member Cooper, and seconded by Member Nye, that the application
be partially approved and partially denied. The motion was to approve removal of the Pepper
tree, and Kumquat tree, noting the Birch tree was moot because it was already removed; deny
the application for removal of the two large King palms; approve the applicant’s request to
plant the King palm as the approved street trees; and approve a payment of $1,500 to the Tree
Bank. The motion was passed unanimously by a roll call vote.

  3. PC-CTP-14-21; Concept Plan for the area located at the intersection of Via Del Monte
  and Via Pinale

Applicant: Rainville Design Studio, 1632 Aviation Blvd., Redondo Beach, CA 90278

The Urban Forester provided the staff report indicating the Malaga Cove Homeowners
Association Beautification Committee is requesting consideration of a conceptual plan for
change to the Parklands pursuant to the Parklands Use Policy and the Change to Parklands
Application Guidelines. Rainville Design Studio proposes landscaping the area with primary
native plants and walking paths for public use providing an alternative to pedestrians to access
the library plaza. He provided history on the current landscaping noting that after 35 years the
median is now very “tired” and need a change. One of the initial landscape plants, Pride of

  3
 Madeira, became invasive and the Bougainvillea has now covered anything that was in its way.
Underneath the Bougainvillea was another shrub that was completely covered creating an
inaccessible median that has a lot of safety issues for visibility of the stop sign and parking.

The Urban Forester presented a rendering of the concept plan indicating all plants will be
removed except the two Canary Island Date palms and the Peruvian Pepper. The entire
perimeter will have a three-foot wide wood chip path; an additional five-foot wide path covered
with wood chips is set back away from the curb and will be lined with small rocks. The plan
will be almost totally native plants that are very attractive and low water use. He depicted the
sloped topography of the triangle. The Malaga Cove Homeowners Association will fund the
project and have a professional do the demolition and installation with volunteer labor from
local residents. There will be increased visibility with the removal of the plants on the median
which will be a benefit to the safety of the street and will improve the aesthetics. The project
schedule will depend on the approved final plan. The Beautification Committee of the
Homeowners Association would like to proceed as soon as the funding is secured and the
proposed plan is finalized and approved by the City Council.

The Concept Plan, if approved, will be returned as a Proposed Plan for the Parklands Committee
to review. The Committee’s recommendations will be incorporated into the proposed plan that
will become final. The Committee will consider the Parklands Use Policy and the Change of
Parklands Application Guidelines in review of this Concept Plan. The Urban Forester stated
that staff recommends approval of the Concept Plan with modification to direct the Malaga
Cove Homeowners Association to prepare a proposed plan modifying or eliminating the interior
pathways to significantly reduce the degree of slope or grading requirements, widen the
perimeter path, and incorporate any comments from the Parklands Committee.

The Committee asked for clarification on the modification or elimination of pathways to which
the Urban Forester responded that he didn’t believe the concept was drawn on a site visit. He
felt it would be difficult to put paths in that steep area lined with rocks and not have rocks rolling
down into the street. There would need to be a lot of grading which would increase the cost
and he didn’t believe a pathway would work when there was a two to one slope. He felt they
would have to work with the topography that exists.

Public Hearing. Chad McAllister on behalf of Applicant Palos Verdes Homeowners
Association addressed the Committee. A lengthy discussion took place with the applicant
regarding the topography and the pathways. Mr. McAllister described ways in which the
pathways could meander so as to work with the topography and noted that until the site is
cleared, there was no way of knowing what the slope really was and how the paths might need
to be adjusted.

Resident Kelly Miller addressed the Committee regarding her concerns about the loss of privacy
with the removal of the current landscaping, and lack of input from the community.

Further discussion ensued to determine how the Malaga Cove Homeowners Association plans
to include input from the entire community.

  4
 Action: Moved by Member Rhodes, and seconded by Member Nye, to approve the Conceptual
plan with the modifications recommended by staff. The motion was approved unanimously.

Notification. These matters have been agenized and posted in the routine manner.
